questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Malaria : Female Anopheles mosquito
2. Kala-azar : Sandfly
3. Dengue : Aedes aegypti mosquito
4. Japanese encephalitis : Aedes aegypti mosquito
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 to 3 are correct. Japanese encephalitis is a viral disease spread mainly by Culex mosquitoes, which breed in paddy fields and are linked to pigs and water birds, while Aedes carries dengue and chikungunya.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Human Health and Disease
questions.h: Aedes = dengue by day; Culex = encephalitis and filaria

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas.
2. Glucagon acts to raise the blood glucose level.
3. A deficiency of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) causes diabetes mellitus.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Lack of ADH causes diabetes insipidus, with large volumes of dilute urine, whereas diabetes mellitus is due to a shortage of insulin or poor response to it. Insulin and glucagon are opposing hormones that keep blood sugar in range.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chemical Coordination and Integration

questions.q:
Statement-I: Vaccination produces active immunity, whereas an injection of antiserum produces passive immunity.
Statement-II: Vaccines stimulate the body's own cells to make antibodies and memory cells, whereas antiserum supplies ready-made antibodies.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Because a vaccinated person's own immune system is trained, protection lasts long, but antiserum protection is quick and short-lived. That is why antiserum is used for emergencies such as snakebite or tetanus.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Human Health and Disease

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Hepatitis A and hepatitis E are mainly spread through contaminated food and water.
2. Hepatitis B and C are spread mainly through blood and body fluids.
3. A vaccine is available for hepatitis C.
4. Hepatitis A is caused by a bacterium.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Hepatitis C has no vaccine yet, though it can now be cured with antiviral drugs, and all hepatitis viruses are viruses, not bacteria.
questions.s: WHO fact sheets; NCERT Class XII Biology

questions.q: Which vitamin contains the metal cobalt, and its deficiency leads to pernicious anaemia?
questions.e: Cyanocobalamin (B12) contains cobalt and is made only by microorganisms, and animal foods supply it. Deficiency impairs red blood cell formation, causing anaemia.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Biology; General Science

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about chromosomal disorders:
1. Down syndrome is caused by trisomy of chromosome 18.
2. Turner syndrome is caused by the presence of only one X chromosome in females (45, XO).
3. Klinefelter syndrome affects males who have an extra X chromosome (47, XXY).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Down syndrome is trisomy 21, and trisomy 18 causes Edwards syndrome. Turner females are short with underdeveloped ovaries, and Klinefelter males have an extra X.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Principles of Inheritance and Variation

questions.q: Apart from the nucleus, which cell organelles contain their own DNA?
questions.e: Mitochondria and chloroplasts have a circular DNA and their own ribosomes, which supports the idea that they arose from bacteria. In humans mitochondrial DNA is passed down almost entirely from the mother.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Biology, Cell: The Unit of Life

questions.q: The South-East Asia Region of the World Health Organization, including India, was certified polio-free in:
questions.e: India's last case was reported in January 2011, and after three years without a case the WHO certified the region polio-free in March 2014. The 2011 date marks the last case, not the certification.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about semiconductors:
1. An n-type semiconductor is made by doping silicon with a pentavalent impurity such as phosphorus.
2. In a p-type semiconductor, holes are the majority charge carriers.
3. The conductivity of a pure semiconductor decreases as its temperature rises.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Heat frees more electrons from bonds in a pure semiconductor, so its conductivity rises with temperature, unlike metals. Pentavalent atoms donate extra electrons, while trivalent atoms such as boron create holes.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Physics, Semiconductor Electronics

questions.q:
Statement-I: A light-emitting diode (LED) glows when it is reverse biased.
Statement-II: An LED is a p-n junction diode in which electron-hole recombination under forward bias releases energy as light.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: An LED emits light only under forward bias, when recombination at the junction gives off photons. The Nobel Prize in Physics for 2014 went to the inventors of the efficient blue LED, which made white LED lighting possible.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Physics, Semiconductor Electronics

questions.q: Which of the following logic gates are called 'universal gates' because any other logic gate can be built from them?
questions.e: Any Boolean function can be implemented using only NAND gates or only NOR gates. That is why they are the preferred building blocks in integrated circuits.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Physics, Semiconductor Electronics

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about optical fibres:
1. They work on the principle of total internal reflection.
2. The core has a lower refractive index than the cladding.
3. They are not affected by electromagnetic interference.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Total internal reflection at the core-cladding boundary needs the core to be denser, with a higher refractive index. Charles Kao won a share of the 2009 Nobel Prize in Physics for the use of glass fibre in communication.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Physics, Ray Optics

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a characteristic of laser light?
o: It spreads widely as a divergent beam, like light from an ordinary bulb
questions.e: Laser light, produced by stimulated emission, has waves in step with one another, a single wavelength and very little divergence. Ordinary bulb light is incoherent, mixed in colour and spreads in all directions.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Physics, Atoms / Dual Nature

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the semiconductor ecosystem in India:
1. The India Semiconductor Mission was launched in 2021 under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
2. Micron's unit at Sanand, Gujarat is meant for assembly, testing, marking and packaging of chips.
3. Micron's Sanand unit is a wafer fabrication plant that makes silicon wafers.
4. The India Semiconductor Mission was launched in 2014.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The mission was approved in December 2021, not 2014, and the Sanand unit is an assembly and packaging (ATMP) facility rather than a wafer fab.

questions.q: Section 66A of the Information Technology Act, 2000, which penalised sending 'offensive' messages online, was struck down by the Supreme Court in:
o: K. S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017)
Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India (2020)
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015)
questions.e: The Court held the section vague and a violation of freedom of speech under Article 19(1)(a), while upholding the blocking power under Section 69A. Puttaswamy dealt with privacy, and Anuradha Bhasin with internet shutdowns.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. CERT-In is the national agency for responding to cyber security incidents under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
2. The National Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Centre is the nodal agency for protecting critical information infrastructure and functions under the National Technical Research Organisation.
3. CERT-In functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: CERT-In, set up under Section 70B of the IT Act, sits in MeitY, while the NCIIPC is created under Section 70A and works under the NTRO. The MHA is not the parent of CERT-In.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023:
1. It provides for the establishment of the Data Protection Board of India.
2. It applies to personal data kept only on paper and never digitised.
3. It uses the terms 'Data Principal' for the individual and 'Data Fiduciary' for the entity that determines how data is processed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Act covers digital personal data, including non-digital data that is later digitised, but not data that stays on paper. It followed the Puttaswamy judgment, which made privacy part of Article 21.

questions.q: In a blockchain, tampering with a past record is easily detected because:
o: each block contains the cryptographic hash of the previous block, so changing one block breaks the links that follow
each block stores the passwords of all users in plain text
a single central server regularly overwrites older blocks
the blocks are stored only on the computer of the first user
questions.e: A hash changes completely if even one character of the block changes, and the next block's stored hash would then no longer match. Because the ledger is copied across many nodes, an altered copy is rejected.
questions.s: Standard IT references; RBI / MeitY explainers

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Supervised learning : Learning from data that comes with correct labels
2. Unsupervised learning : Finding patterns in data without labels
3. Reinforcement learning : Learning through rewards and penalties for actions taken
4. Deep learning : Learning that works only with a single-layer neural network
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 to 3 are correct. Deep learning uses neural networks with many layers, which is what 'deep' refers to, and so the fourth is wrong.
questions.s: Standard IT references; IndiaAI Mission explainers

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about quantum technology:
1. A qubit can exist in a superposition of the states 0 and 1.
2. India's National Quantum Mission, approved in 2023, is implemented through the Department of Science and Technology.
3. In quantum key distribution, an eavesdropper can read the key without disturbing the quantum states.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Measurement disturbs a quantum state, so an eavesdropper on a quantum key exchange leaves detectable traces, which is the security advantage of the method. The mission covers computing, communication, sensing and materials.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Li-Fi transmits data using visible light.
Statement-II: Li-Fi signals can pass through walls, so it offers wider indoor coverage than Wi-Fi.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Li-Fi sends data by rapidly varying the intensity of LED light, but light is blocked by walls, so coverage is limited to the lit area. This limited range is a drawback, though it also makes the link harder to intercept from outside.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's digital public infrastructure:
1. The Unified Payments Interface is operated directly by the Reserve Bank of India.
2. The Open Network for Digital Commerce is an initiative of the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade.
3. UIDAI is a statutory authority under the Aadhaar Act, 2016.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: UPI is run by the National Payments Corporation of India, an umbrella organisation promoted by the RBI and banks, and not by the RBI itself. UIDAI got its statutory status through the Aadhaar Act, 2016.

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT developed under the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP) launched in 1983?
questions.e: The IGMDP under Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam produced Prithvi, Agni, Trishul, Akash and Nag. BrahMos is a joint venture between DRDO and Russia's NPO Mashinostroyeniya, and it is a supersonic cruise missile.
questions.h: P-A-T-A-N: Prithvi, Agni, Trishul, Akash, Nag

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. BrahMos is a supersonic cruise missile developed by a joint venture between India and Russia.
2. Astra is a surface-to-air missile.
3. Pinaka is a multi-barrel rocket launcher system.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Astra is a beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile, fired from fighter aircraft such as the Su-30MKI and the Tejas. Surface-to-air missiles include the Akash.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Mission Divyastra test of Agni-5 in March 2024 demonstrated India's capability in MIRV technology.
Statement-II: Agni-5 has a range of more than 5,000 kilometres.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: MIRV means that one missile carries several warheads that can be aimed at different targets. Agni-5's long range is a separate fact and does not explain MIRV capability.

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes a cruise missile from a ballistic missile?
o: A cruise missile follows a free-fall arc outside the atmosphere, whereas a ballistic missile flies using jet engines throughout
A cruise missile is powered and steered through most of its flight within the atmosphere, while a ballistic missile follows a free-fall arc after a short powered phase
A cruise missile can only be launched from submarines, whereas a ballistic missile can only be launched from land
A cruise missile always carries a nuclear warhead, whereas a ballistic missile never does
questions.e: Ballistic missiles are boosted by rocket motors for a short time and then follow a trajectory under gravity, but cruise missiles such as BrahMos fly like pilotless aircraft on air-breathing engines. Either type can carry conventional or nuclear warheads and can be launched from various platforms.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India and export control regimes:
1. India became a member of the Missile Technology Control Regime in 2016.
2. India became a member of the Wassenaar Arrangement in 2017.
3. India is a full member of the Nuclear Suppliers Group.
4. India became a member of the Australia Group in 2018.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India entered MTCR in June 2016, Wassenaar in December 2017 and the Australia Group in January 2018. Its NSG membership bid, opposed mainly by China, remains pending.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about INS Vikrant:
1. It is the first aircraft carrier built in India, constructed at Cochin Shipyard Limited and commissioned in 2022.
2. It uses a catapult-assisted take-off arrangement (CATOBAR).
3. The other operational carrier of India, INS Vikramaditya, was acquired from Russia.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Vikrant uses a ski-jump with arrestor wires (STOBAR), not catapults. Vikramaditya is the former Soviet carrier Admiral Gorshkov, refitted in Russia.

questions.q: The sea leg of India's nuclear triad is provided by:
o: INS Arihant class nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarines
INS Vikrant, the indigenous aircraft carrier
INS Vikramaditya, the carrier acquired from Russia
questions.e: A credible second-strike capability needs submarines that can stay hidden underwater for long periods with ballistic missiles, which nuclear propulsion allows. Kalvari-class submarines are conventional attack boats.

questions.q: Mission Shakti, conducted by India in March 2019, was a demonstration of:
o: an anti-satellite capability, by destroying a satellite in low Earth orbit with a ground-launched interceptor
the first crewed orbital flight of an Indian astronaut
a hypersonic cruise missile with a scramjet engine
India's second series of nuclear tests at Pokhran
questions.e: A DRDO interceptor hit an Indian satellite at an altitude of about 300 km, which made India the fourth country with this capability. The 1998 Pokhran tests were Operation Shakti, a different event.

questions.q:
Match List-I (technique) with List-II (molecule detected):
A. Southern blotting
B. Northern blotting
C. Western blotting
1. RNA
2. DNA
3. Protein
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Southern blotting, named after Edwin Southern, detects DNA, and the names Northern and Western were then coined for RNA and protein. These techniques separate molecules by gel electrophoresis and then probe them on a membrane.

questions.q: The ELISA test, used for the initial screening of infections such as HIV, is based on:
o: binding of an antigen to its specific antibody, detected by an enzyme-linked antibody that produces a colour change
amplification of target DNA by a heat-stable polymerase
separation of DNA fragments by size in an electric field
hybridisation of a labelled DNA probe to DNA on a membrane
questions.e: ELISA looks for antibodies or antigens, not the pathogen's genetic material, and a positive result is usually confirmed by another test. PCR, gel electrophoresis and Southern blotting are the other three options respectively.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Human Health and Disease

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about antimicrobial resistance:
1. Overuse and misuse of antibiotics select for resistant bacteria.
2. Antibiotics are effective in the treatment of viral infections such as influenza.
3. Resistance genes can spread between bacteria through plasmids.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Antibiotics act on bacterial structures and do not work on viruses, so using them for flu only adds to selection pressure. Plasmids can carry resistance genes from one bacterium to another, even across species.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Human Health and Disease

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about microbes in medicine and industry:
1. Streptokinase, produced by Streptococcus, is used as a clot buster.
2. Cyclosporin A, obtained from a fungus, is used as an immunosuppressant in organ transplants.
3. Statins, obtained from the yeast Monascus purpureus, lower blood cholesterol.
4. Citric acid is commercially produced by Lactobacillus.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 to 3 are correct. Citric acid is produced by the fungus Aspergillus niger, and Lactobacillus is linked to lactic acid and curd.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Microbes in Human Welfare

questions.q: The microbes that produce methane in biogas plants from cattle dung belong to:
questions.e: Methanogens such as Methanobacterium are strict anaerobes that live in the rumen of cattle and in the sludge of biogas plants. They form the methane-rich gas that is used as fuel.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Microbes in Human Welfare

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Lactobacillus converts milk into curd by producing lactic acid that coagulates milk proteins.
2. Curd has a higher vitamin B12 content than milk.
3. The large holes in Swiss cheese are due to methane released by Lactobacillus.
4. Roquefort cheese is ripened by specific bacteria rather than fungi.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The holes in Swiss cheese come from carbon dioxide produced by Propionibacterium shermanii, and Roquefort is ripened by a fungus.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Microbes in Human Welfare

questions.q: A foreign DNA fragment is inserted at the BamHI site of the cloning vector pBR322, which lies within the tetracycline resistance gene. Bacteria carrying this recombinant plasmid will be:
o: resistant to tetracycline but sensitive to ampicillin
resistant to both ampicillin and tetracycline
sensitive to both ampicillin and tetracycline
resistant to ampicillin but sensitive to tetracycline
questions.e: The insert disrupts the tetracycline gene, which is called insertional inactivation, while the ampicillin gene stays intact. This lets scientists pick recombinant colonies by growing them on different antibiotic plates.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Biotechnology: Principles and Processes

questions.q: FELUDA, a low-cost diagnostic test developed by Indian scientists and approved for COVID-19 detection, is based on:
o: reverse transcription PCR using a heat-stable polymerase
CRISPR-Cas technology, using FnCas9 on a paper strip
sequencing of the viral genome with nanopores
questions.e: FELUDA was developed by CSIR-IGIB and uses a Cas9 protein to detect the target viral sequence, with the result seen as lines on a paper strip. It is notable as an Indian application of CRISPR in diagnostics.

questions.q: The size of colloidal particles lies approximately between:
questions.e: Colloids fall between true solutions and suspensions, and this scattering of light by colloid particles is the Tyndall effect. Nanoparticles at the lower end of this range often form colloidal sols.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Chemistry, Surface Chemistry

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about nanotechnology in agriculture:
1. Nanosensors can be used to detect pesticide residues or pathogens in crops and soil.
2. Nano-encapsulation can allow slow and targeted release of agrochemicals.
3. Nano-pesticides have removed all concerns about environmental contamination.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Nanocarriers can cut dosage and run-off, but the fate of the nanoparticles in soil and water is still under study. The claim that all concerns have been removed is therefore not justified.

questions.q: Liposomes, widely studied in nanomedicine, are:
o: spherical vesicles made of a phospholipid bilayer that can carry drugs in their core or membrane
rods of carbon atoms rolled into a tube
crystals of semiconductor that glow when excited
long chains of silica used as optical fibres
questions.e: Water-soluble drugs sit in the watery core, and fat-soluble drugs sit in the lipid layer. Liposomal formulations of some cancer drugs reduce side effects on healthy tissue.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Biology, Cell; DST

questions.q:
Statement-I: Some nanomaterials can be more toxic than the same substance in bulk form.
Statement-II: Their small size and large surface area let them react more readily and enter cells more easily.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The properties that make nanomaterials useful, namely high surface reactivity and small size, are the same ones that raise concerns. Toxicity therefore has to be tested for each nanoform, rather than assumed from the bulk.

questions.q: Nanofiltration membranes, used in water treatment, are best described as:
o: having pores larger than a micrometre, removing only visible sand particles
allowing only water molecules to pass, as in perfect desalination
removing only dissolved gases such as oxygen and nitrogen
having pores of about a nanometre, intermediate between ultrafiltration and reverse osmosis, and removing mainly divalent ions such as those causing hardness
questions.e: Nanofiltration can soften water by retaining calcium and magnesium while letting many monovalent ions pass, and it needs lower pressure than reverse osmosis.

questions.q: The ability of a gecko to cling to walls and ceilings is explained by:
o: tiny suction cups on its toe pads
a sticky glue secreted from glands on its feet
static electricity built up in its skin
billions of nanoscale spatulae on its foot hairs (setae) that give van der Waals adhesion
questions.e: Millions of setae, each ending in hundreds of nanoscale spatulae, bring the foot extremely close to the surface, and the weak van der Waals forces add up. This inspired dry adhesives.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO):
1. It is a specialised agency of the United Nations.
2. It functions as part of the secretariat of the World Trade Organization.
3. It publishes the Global Innovation Index along with partner institutions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: WIPO is headquartered in Geneva and administers treaties such as Berne, Paris and the PCT, but it is separate from the WTO, which administers TRIPS. It became a UN specialised agency in 1974.

questions.q: Which one of the following can be patented in India, provided it meets the requirements of novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability?
o: A novel, non-naturally occurring micro-organism with a new industrial use
A new variety of rice plant as such
A method of treating a human patient by surgery
The mere discovery of a new property of a known substance
questions.e: Plants and animals other than micro-organisms, methods of medical treatment and the mere discovery of a new property (Section 3(d)) are all excluded. Micro-organisms are patentable, in line with TRIPS.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The owner of a registered trade mark can sue for infringement when another person uses a deceptively similar mark for similar goods.
Statement-II: Trade mark law aims to prevent consumers from being confused about the origin of goods.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The test is whether an ordinary buyer of average memory could be misled, so an exact copy is not needed to infringe. The purpose of preventing confusion is what justifies the right against similar marks.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Under the TRIPS Agreement, Geographical Indications for wines and spirits receive a higher level of protection than those for other products.
Statement-II: India has been among the countries seeking the extension of this higher level of protection to other products.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Article 23 gives the additional protection to wines and spirits, while Article 22 gives the basic level to all goods. India's demand is a negotiating position, and it does not explain the existing difference.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. The Trade Marks Act
2. The Copyright Act
3. The coming into force of the TRIPS Agreement
4. The Patents Act
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Copyright Act is of 1957, the Patents Act of 1970, the TRIPS Agreement came into force with the WTO in 1995, and the present Trade Marks Act was enacted in 1999. TRIPS compliance drove the later amendments.

questions.q: The Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks, who heads the Indian Patent Office, functions under the:
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
questions.e: DPIIT is the nodal department for IPR policy and administration, and the patent, design, trade mark and GI offices all operate under the CGPDTM. The Copyright Office is also under DPIIT now.
